Full marks may be obtained for answers to ALL questions. Mathematical formulae booklets published by the GCE Board are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving the answer at each stage. Calculators are allowed. Start each question on a fresh page.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The equation of a curve $C$ is given by
$$y = \frac{x}{3}(x^2 - 4).$$
Find $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ at the point $P(-1, 1)$. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Expand first: $y = \dfrac{x^3 - 4x}{3}$, so
$$\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{3x^2 - 4}{3} = x^2 - \frac43.$$
(Check that $P$ is on $C$: $y = \frac{-1}{3}(1 - 4) = 1$.) At $x = -1$:
$$\boxed{\frac{dy}{dx} = 1 - \frac43 = -\frac13}$$

questions.enonce_markdown: The curve $C$ has equation $y = \dfrac{x}{3}(x^2 - 4)$. Find the equation of the tangent $T$ to $C$ at the point $P(-1, 1)$. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
The gradient of $T$ is $\left.\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right|_{x=-1} = -\dfrac13$ (part (a)). Using $y - y_1 = m(x - x_1)$ at $(-1, 1)$:
$$y - 1 = -\frac13(x + 1) \;\Rightarrow\; 3y - 3 = -x - 1.$$
$$\boxed{x + 3y = 2} \qquad\left(\text{equivalently } y = \tfrac{2 - x}{3}\right)$$

questions.enonce_markdown: The curve $C$ has equation $y = \dfrac{x}{3}(x^2 - 4)$ and the tangent $T$ to $C$ at $P(-1, 1)$ has equation $x + 3y = 2$. Find the coordinates of the point $Q$, where the tangent $T$ meets $C$ again. (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Substitute $3y = x^3 - 4x$ (from the curve) into $x + 3y = 2$:
$$x + x^3 - 4x = 2 \;\Rightarrow\; x^3 - 3x - 2 = 0.$$
Because $T$ touches $C$ at $P$, $x = -1$ is a repeated root, so $(x + 1)^2$ is a factor:
$$x^3 - 3x - 2 = (x + 1)(x^2 - x - 2) = (x + 1)(x + 1)(x - 2) = (x + 1)^2(x - 2).$$
The other intersection has $x = 2$. Then $y = \dfrac{2}{3}(2^2 - 4) = 0$ (and on the tangent, $y = \dfrac{2 - 2}{3} = 0$, which agrees).
$$\boxed{Q = (2,\, 0)}$$

questions.enonce_markdown:
Given that $f(x) = \dfrac{3x}{(x - 1)(x + 2)}$, $x \in \mathbb{R} \setminus \{-2, 1\}$,

(d) express $f(x)$ into partial fractions.

(e) find $\displaystyle\int f(x)\,dx$. (6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(d) Partial fractions.** Write
$$\frac{3x}{(x - 1)(x + 2)} \equiv \frac{A}{x - 1} + \frac{B}{x + 2} \;\Rightarrow\; 3x \equiv A(x + 2) + B(x - 1).$$
Put $x = 1$: $3 = 3A$, so $A = 1$. Put $x = -2$: $-6 = -3B$, so $B = 2$.
$$\boxed{f(x) = \frac{1}{x - 1} + \frac{2}{x + 2}}$$
Check at $x = 2$: $f(2) = \dfrac{6}{4} = \dfrac32$ and $\dfrac11 + \dfrac24 = \dfrac32$.

**(e) Integration.** Integrate term by term:
$$\int f(x)\,dx = \int\frac{dx}{x - 1} + 2\int\frac{dx}{x + 2} = \ln|x - 1| + 2\ln|x + 2| + C.$$
$$\boxed{\int f(x)\,dx = \ln|x - 1| + 2\ln|x + 2| + C = \ln\left|(x - 1)(x + 2)^2\right| + C}$$
